skill.name: image-to-video
skill.description: Routes image-to-video requests to HappyHorse, Wan, or Seedance models and prepares model-specific prompts and RunComfy CLI inputs.
skill.summary: Create short videos from still images with intent-based RunComfy model selection.
skill.author: skills-collective

security_audit.summary: All 67 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown formatting, documented URLs, URL placeholders, and a documented configuration path. Semantic review identified unsafe shell quoting guidance, unpinned package installation, and third-party transmission of prompts and media URLs.

remediation.issue: The examples place user-controlled JSON inside single-quoted shell commands while claiming prompt content has no shell injection surface.
remediation.suggestion: Require JSON serialization and structured argument invocation without a shell. Remove the safety claim until shell-layer escaping is explicitly enforced.

remediation.issue: The npx and global npm installation commands do not pin package versions or integrity.
remediation.suggestion: Pin reviewed package versions and document a checksum, lockfile, or trusted release verification process.

remediation.issue: The workflow sends prompts and media URLs to RunComfy, which fetches referenced content on remote servers.
remediation.suggestion: Require confirmation before transmitting sensitive content and warn users against private, signed, or internal media URLs.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Shell Interpolation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill claims there is no shell injection surface while showing user-controlled JSON inside single-quoted shell commands. An unescaped apostrophe can terminate the shell string before the CLI receives it.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples directly place JSON in shell single quotes, and line 202 makes a safety claim that only applies after shell parsing.

semantic_findings.title: Unpinned Remote Package Installation
semantic_findings.description: The installation instructions invoke npx and install a global npm package without a version or integrity pin. A compromised later release could execute during installation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both commands are explicitly documented without versions or integrity controls, creating a clear dependency supply-chain exposure.

semantic_findings.title: Third-Party Content Transmission
semantic_findings.description: The workflow sends prompts and user-supplied media URLs to the RunComfy Model API, where remote servers fetch referenced content. Sensitive prompts or private URLs could be disclosed to a third party.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Lines 197 and 203 explicitly state that the CLI posts to the Model API and that RunComfy servers fetch supplied media URLs.

content.value_statement: Choosing an image-to-video model and prompt can waste generation time. This skill routes each request to a suitable RunComfy model and prepares its parameters.
actual_capabilities: Routes general portrait, product, and ambient-audio animations to HappyHorse 1.0 I2V.
Routes custom-audio talking-head requests to Wan 2.7 with audio-driven lip synchronization.
Routes combined image, video, and audio reference requests to Seedance 2.0 Pro.
Prepares model-specific prompts, durations, resolutions, aspect ratios, seeds, and output settings.
Invokes the RunComfy CLI and directs generated files to a selected output directory.
limitations: Requires the RunComfy CLI, an authenticated account, and provider access.
Sends prompts and referenced media URLs to third-party RunComfy services.
Each route creates one clip with model-specific duration, resolution, and format limits.
The Wan custom-audio route generates a talking head but does not consume the original source image.

use_cases.title: Animate Social Portraits
use_cases.description: Turn a portrait into a short vertical clip with subtle facial motion and stable identity.

use_cases.title: Produce Localized Spokesperson Clips
use_cases.description: Generate talking-head variants from separate language audio tracks while keeping framing and visual direction consistent.

use_cases.title: Build Referenced Product Stories
use_cases.description: Combine a product image, movement reference, and audio reference into one directed promotional clip.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Portrait Animation
prompt_templates.prompt: Animate [image URL] for [duration] seconds. Use subtle breathing, one blink, gentle camera drift, stable facial features, and [aspect ratio].

prompt_templates.title: Controlled Product Reveal
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [duration]-second product reveal from [image URL]. Orbit slowly around the product. Preserve packaging text, geometry, colors, and background.

prompt_templates.title: Audio-Driven Spokesperson
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [duration]-second [aspect ratio] talking-head video using [audio URL]. Match the audio timing. Use [framing], [lighting], and no subtitles.

prompt_templates.title: Multimodal Reference Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [image URL] as subject, [video URL] for scene motion, and [audio URL] for voice. Create [duration] seconds and preserve [required details].

output_examples.input: Animate a portrait for five seconds with a slow push-in and natural room sound.
output_examples.output: Selected HappyHorse 1.0 I2V. Prepared a five-second identity-preserving portrait animation with a slow camera push and native ambient audio.

output_examples.input: Create a vertical spokesperson clip that follows my twelve-second voiceover.
output_examples.output: Selected Wan 2.7. Prepared a twelve-second vertical talking-head request with the supplied audio, fixed framing, and subtitles disabled.

output_examples.input: Use my product image, reference clip, and soundtrack to make an eight-second launch video.
output_examples.output: Selected Seedance 2.0 Pro. Assigned the product as the primary image and used the video and audio as numbered references.

best_practices: Use one primary motion beat per clip and describe camera movement before visual details.
State which identity, packaging, geometry, or background details must remain unchanged.
Match duration to reference audio and reuse the seed when comparing controlled variants.
anti_patterns: Do not combine conflicting visual styles across image and video references.
Do not restate every visible image detail when the prompt should describe motion.
Do not expect one route to blend outputs from several models or exceed provider limits.

faq.question: Which model is selected by default?
faq.answer: HappyHorse 1.0 I2V is the default for portraits, products, and general still-image animation.

faq.question: Can I provide my own voiceover?
faq.answer: Yes. The Wan 2.7 route accepts a compatible audio URL for talking-head lip synchronization.

faq.question: Does the Wan route animate my source image?
faq.answer: No. This route generates a talking-head clip from a prompt and audio. Use HappyHorse for direct source-image animation.

faq.question: Can I combine image, video, and audio references?
faq.answer: Yes. Seedance 2.0 Pro accepts multiple reference types within its documented count, duration, and size limits.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Install the RunComfy CLI, authenticate with RunComfy, and provide supported media URLs.

faq.question: Where are generated videos saved?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI downloads completed outputs into the absolute directory supplied for the request.
